records.title: Politics and Cultures of Marketplace Displays in France
records.header: FRENCH 220 Politics and Cultures of Marketplace Displays in France (5) A&H
records.text: FRENCH 220 Politics and Cultures of Marketplace Displays in France (5) A&H Investigates how commercial spaces such as the fresh food market and the department store became fertile terrain for both constructing and critiquing a sense of French national identity. Considers the political significance of food, fashion, and/or other commodities as well as the architectural structures erected to display them. Explores tensions between consumer culture and civic values. Offered: AWSp.

records.text: FRENCH 222 Human and Machine Translation (5) SSc Machine translation's development and implications of its use with an emphasis on the role of humans in machine translation. How machine translation is changing the way translation is approached today. Taught in English, but focuses substantially on materials originally in French. Course overlaps with: TXTDS 222. Recommended: one year of college-level language instruction, proficiency in a heritage language, or equivalent.

records.title: Sex, Commerce, and the Making of Modern Paris
records.header: FRENCH 223 Sex, Commerce, and the Making of Modern Paris (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: FRENCH 223 Sex, Commerce, and the Making of Modern Paris (5) SSc, DIV Explores how Paris became the city of love. Examines how sexual commerce shaped the identity of the city, how the commercial spaces of the city shaped sexual identities, and how discourses about sexuality contributed to the legitimation of capitalism. Topics include the construction of gender difference, the emergence of mass media, and the commercial origins of queer identities.

records.title: Histories and Futures of the Book, Texts and Reading
records.header: FRENCH 224 Histories and Futures of the Book, Texts and Reading (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: FRENCH 224 Histories and Futures of the Book, Texts and Reading (5) A&H/SSc From medieval manuscripts to commercially printed books to today's rapidly recycled digital content, explores how changing forms have shaped the ways texts have been read and understood, how the spread of printing technology impacted the modern world, how the book-form became dominant, and how a new media revolution (the mass digitization of texts) is again reshaping access to and understanding of the past. Offered: jointly with JSIS A 224/TXTDS 224.

records.text: FRENCH 226 The Idea of Europe in French Film (5) SSc/A&H Demonstrates how the European ideal today emerged from a context of extreme conflict. records.header: FRENCH 228 The Water Crisis in Literature and Film (5) SSc/A&H
records.text: FRENCH 228 The Water Crisis in Literature and Film (5) SSc/A&H Interprets a variety of texts (literary, cinematic, etc.) that address the water crisis to understand how water's meaning has changed as people become more conscious of risks in supply (pollution and natural/man-made scarcity) and as access to it is increasingly mediated in light of things like privatization and commodification. Uses an interdisciplinary approach from fields of sociolinguistics, migrant/identity/cultural studies. Considers broad range of examples from interactions between immigrant groups and host countries. records.header: FRENCH 441 Quebecois Literature (5) A&H, DIV
records.text: FRENCH 441 Quebecois Literature (5) A&H, DIV Quebecois novels, short stories, and poetry from both indigenous and non-indigenous authors. Emphasis on francophone First Nations writers in context of their history and cultures. Attention to authors' representation of the land and how it shapes their characters' identities. Includes Quebecois films. In French. Prerequisite: FRENCH 303. Offered: jointly with JSIS A 441.

records.text: FRENCH 448 Cultures of Franco-America (5) SSc/A&H, DIV Considers a broad range of literary and cultural texts emerging from the long history of the French in North America and Americans in France. records.title: Translation Theory and Practice
records.header: FRENCH 472 Translation Theory and Practice (5) A&H
records.text: FRENCH 472 Translation Theory and Practice (5) A&H This course develops advanced translation skills through work on a variety of genres (literary, commercial, journalistic, etc.) and in a variety of modes (interpreting, subtitling, etc.). It also engages translation theory by considering the problem of cultural difference embedded in language and broader issues of originality in and the "ownership" of the translated text. Conducted in French and English. Prerequisite: two of FRENCH 301, FRENCH 302, or FRENCH 303. Offered: W, even years.

records.title: Reading and Writing: Manuscripts in the Middle Ages
records.header: FRENCH 474 Reading and Writing: Manuscripts in the Middle Ages (5) SSc/A&H
records.text: FRENCH 474 Reading and Writing: Manuscripts in the Middle Ages (5) SSc/A&H Production, transmission, and circulation of texts in late medieval France and Italy. Theories and methods used when editing medieval texts. Examines the rising importance of the written word and of cultures of reading for many critical aspects in late medieval French life and their influences on Italian culture at the time. In English.
